result.title: Strength Controls Change How Interventions Compare Across Sparse Autoencoder Codes
result.summary: Changing sparse autoencoder (SAE) codes can alter both intervention direction and magnitude, so comparing intervention effects requires a strength control specifying what is held equal. Norm matching and output calibration provide different controls, but whether interventions yield different effects across codes after strength matching remains unclear. We compare intervention effects under these controls for fixed feature groups in Gemma and Llama and observe: (1) Whole-patch scaling. With one coefficient per input, full-output Kullback-Leibler (KL) calibration leaves smaller mean effect gaps from the encoder-based reference intervention than total-norm matching for nonnegative least-squares (NNLS) refits. On new Llama inputs, total-norm matching loses 11 reference transfers, whereas full-output calibration preserves every transfer decision. (2) Positionwise scaling. On a small matched gender-agreement subset, positionwise norm matching leaves smaller observed mean gaps than full-output calibration. (3) Answer exclusion. Compared with unscaled NNLS, answer-excluded calibration reduces gaps in the measured subject-verb agreement comparisons but increases them for gender refits. Full-output KL calibration also reduces larger gaps for norm-matched constructed candidates, although matching coverage is incomplete in several settings. Since calibration uses the evaluated input's outputs, it serves as a diagnostic of residual disagreement.

AI.brief_summary: 论文比较稀疏自编码器（SAE）特征干预在不同强度控制（总范数匹配与全输出 KL 校准）下的效果差异，在 Gemma 与 Llama 上考察整段与逐位置缩放、答案排除等设定，并指出输出校准可诊断残余分歧。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「干预强度如何对齐」的对照方案可能供核查 latent 状态编辑、激活替换类因果贡献比较时的强度混杂问题；但对象为纯文本 SAE 特征干预，与视觉细节保留和推理状态生成无直接联系，迁移线索需人工判断。
